note: Canonical peerDependencies range for @deepseek-ai/dsh-* across the ecosystem. The OR form is required by semver's prerelease rule: a prerelease version only satisfies a comparator set when a comparator in the same [major, minor, patch] tuple carries a prerelease, so 0.1.5-rc.1 is NOT admitted by the bare '>=0.1.2-rc.1 <0.2.0'. Every new upstream prerelease tuple needs its own clause - run `node scripts/check-peer-range-latest.mjs` to detect a missing one (it reads the published dist-tags and prints the clause to append). The third clause covers the 0.1.6 tuple with a '-0' floor, the same shape the tripwire suggests (never the bare '>=0.1.6' form): it admits every 0.1.6 prerelease including 0.1.6-alpha.2. The fourth clause covers the 0.1.7 tuple the same way (0.1.7-rc.2 was the previous verified line): it admits every 0.1.7 prerelease, which the three-clause form excludes because its newest comparator sits on the 0.1.6 tuple. The fifth and sixth clauses open the 0.2 corridor and are the first ones whose upper bound is not <0.2.0 - the old upper bound excluded every 0.2.x version, so the 0.2.1-alpha.1 host line is rejected by the four-clause form. They keep the same '-0' floor shape: `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0` admits the 0.2.0 tuple (the published `next`/`latest` line) and `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0` admits the 0.2.1 tuple (the verified `alpha` line); both are needed because semver's prerelease rule keys on the exact [major, minor, patch] tuple, and the tripwire checks every dist-tag. Older clauses are never dropped: the peer range stays wider than the verified line so installs on the 0.1.x corridor keep working. Run `node scripts/sync-peer-range.mjs --dir <reposDir> --write` after updating this file to re-pin every repo, then let the shared Renovate preset open the update PRs.
